images.title: Divisible by 6 and by 4 means divisible by 12
images.purpose: Shows on a number line that the numbers divisible by both 6 and 4 come every 12, not every 24.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One long number line across the middle with dots above and below and four rings.
images.exact_structure: A horizontal number line from 0 to 48 with 25 short ticks, one at every even number; only 0, 12, 24, 36 and 48 carry numerals. Above the line, 8 teal (#0072B2) dots at 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, with the label multiples of 6 at the left above them. Below the line, 12 amber (#E69F00) dots at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48, with the label multiples of 4 at the left below them. Exactly 4 reddish purple (#CC79A7) rings, at 12, 24, 36 and 48, each enclosing the teal dot and the amber dot at that number. Under the line at the right: common: every 12. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Divisible by both 6 and 4 means divisible by their LCM, 12, not by 24.
images.description: Shows on a number line that the numbers divisible by both 6 and 4 come every 12, not every 24.
images.teaching_notes: The 9 and 4 case (LCM 36) is in the video.

image_decisions.why: Two rows of multiples meeting every 12 make the LCM rule visible.
